10-16.text: Abolitionist John Brown led a raid on the federal armory at Harpers Ferry, hoping to spark an uprising against slavery. The raid helped push the country closer to the Civil War.
The Cardiff Giant, a supposed petrified giant, was uncovered on a New York farm. It was a hoax, but thousands of people paid to see it.
President William Howard Taft met Mexican President Porfirio Díaz in the first summit between presidents of the two countries. An assassination plot was also uncovered.
Margaret Sanger opened the first birth control clinic in the United States, challenging laws restricting access to contraception.
Walt Disney and his brother Roy founded the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio, the beginning of what would become the Walt Disney Company.
Chinese Communist forces began the Long March, a grueling retreat that helped shape the country’s political future.
Nazi authorities established the Warsaw Ghetto in occupied Poland, eventually confining hundreds of thousands of Jewish people there.
Ten Nazi leaders convicted at the Nuremberg trials were executed for their roles in World War Two atrocities.
President John F. Kennedy was briefed on photographs of Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba, beginning a confrontation that brought the world close to nuclear war.
Olympic medalists Tommie Smith and John Carlos were expelled from the U.S. team after raising their fists on the medal stand in a protest against racial injustice.
The Million Man March drew a huge crowd to Washington, D.C., for a gathering focused on Black unity, responsibility, and community action.
A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck the Mojave Desert in Southern California. Its remote location helped limit the damage.

10-17.text: British General John Burgoyne surrendered his army at Saratoga, giving the Americans a major Revolutionary War victory and helping persuade France to join their cause.
Chicago gangster Al Capone was convicted of federal income tax evasion. The verdict ultimately sent one of America’s most notorious mob bosses to prison.
Mother Teresa was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her work helping the poor and sick in India.
The Loma Prieta earthquake struck Northern California during the World Series, shaking the San Francisco Bay Area and interrupting the live baseball broadcast.
Canada legalized recreational cannabis nationwide, becoming one of the first countries to do so.
